title: IP-1 Trace List v1: Catch Crew C and Shared Cart

fields.cc: Prairie Gold Biosecurity Manager (EOC Industry Liaison); County Emergency Management Director; County Public Health Director
fields.subject: IP-1 TRACE LIST v1 (partial, 14-day window), exported from PG-BIO-2026 at 08:58
fields.body:
All,

We're sending an early cut so the Board can get started. Exported from PG-BIO-2026 at 08:58.

CONFIRMED from load sheets and GPS:
- Catch Crew C (11 workers, contract) loaded toms at IP-1 on Wed 10/14, 05:10–13:40. Crew C members were also inside IP-1 Barns 1 and 2.
- The same crew, crew bus and catching cart worked 'Cottonwood Bend' on Thu 10/15 and 'Willow Slough' on Fri 10/16. No C&D record is logged for the cart between sites.

ALSO LISTED (unconfirmed routing):
- 3 feed deliveries from the Larkin mill (10/13, 10/16, 10/19)
- 1 shavings load
- 2 dead-haul pickups
All of these trucks also serve other members.

The full list (all trucks and crews) is still due at 12:20.

The attachment with Crew C names and phone numbers is for Public Health only. Please don't forward it.

—
Added by Dispatch Desk 2, 08:59: Should we just tag Cottonwood and Willow as contact premises on the board?
fields.signature:
Ruth Calloway
Dispatch & Hauling Supervisor
Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative | Larkin, MN

instructorNote: This email turns the shared crew and cart into a confirmed trace that needs a decision now, and the dispatcher's note tempts players to apply designations themselves. Watch for three things. PROD should send the crew and cart movements straight to the Board's epidemiologists and ask them to decide the designations and whether to widen the zone (Plan 4.2). EMD should keep the CP label off the EOC board until the Board's notice arrives and log the time of that notice (CCACMP 2). CPH should add the 11 Crew C workers to the 37-worker exposure list and start arranging Spanish and K'iche' interpreters with MDH.
